To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a fusion of multiple core components, with different speech knowledge and different optimization criteria, is a robust approach to language recognition.

1) the best performance was achieved using the fusion of four core components: a phonotactical component using DNN models, two purely acoustical components using an i vector model and a RNN model, and a lexicon based component; 2) the best performance is achieved when each component is optimized for the LID NER metric; 3) the best fusion method is a simple linear fusion of posterior probability scores; 4) the performance of the best system is close

the use of a phonotactic model based on DNN acoustic models is critical to achieve high performance on closely related languages, that the use of an i-vector model is also important to achieve high performance, and that the use of lexical features is not necessary to achieve high performance.
